summary: The Universal Credit Act 2025 aims to alter the rates of the standard allowance, limited capability for work element, and limited capability for work and work-related activity element of universal credit.
Key definitions include 'pre-2026 claimant', 'severe conditions criteria claimant', and 'limited capability for work and work-related activity'.
Eligibility for universal credit is based on various factors, including income, capability for work, and work-related activity.
The Secretary of State has obligations to exercise relevant powers to secure the standard allowance and limited capability for work and work-related activity elements.
The Act includes enforcement elements, such as the power to increase certain amounts to achieve specific results.
The Act specifies payment calculations and entitlement structures for universal credit and employment and support allowance.
Record-keeping requirements are implied through the need to track assessment periods and benefit weeks.
The Act includes corresponding provisions for Northern Ireland.
The Act may be cited as the Universal Credit Act 2025.
